harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: LDAP field-level privacy is deployed and persistent. From node2, anonymous users receive no employee records; the directory reader sees Morgan Lake’s name and mail but not employeeNumber and cannot modify it; the HR administrator can read and change employeeNumber. Both nodes were rebooted serially and recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL-compatible 389 Directory Server 3.2 on node1 and LDAP clients on both nodes without changing the OS release or kernel.
Loaded the supplied HR LDIF and retained the original files under /srv/legacy2/ldap-attribute-privacy.
Created dedicated directory-reader and HR administrator identities. Root-only credentials are stored under /root/ldap-demo on both nodes with 0700/0600 permissions.
Applied scoped ACIs for public employee fields and administrator-only employeeNumber access.
Enabled certificate-validated LDAPS and restricted LDAP/LDAPS ingress on node1 to node2's IP while retaining SELinux enforcing and firewalld.
Verified administrator modification by changing employeeNumber temporarily and restoring HR-4815.
Removed temporary credential-transfer keys, LDIFs, test files, and rollback residue.
Safely rebooted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified service, data, access policy, credentials, and source records after recovery.

evidence.requirement: Supplied LDIF loaded and original records retained
evidence.summary: The supplied suffix and Morgan employee entry were loaded; the retained LDIF has matching SHA-256 bbfcee87...dd10f on both nodes after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Reader can search employee names and mail from node2 without seeing employeeNumber
evidence.summary: Remote LDAPS searches return Morgan Lake and morgan@hr.test while omitting employeeNumber, both before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Only HR administrator may read or change employeeNumber
evidence.summary: Configured ACIs are shown; reader modification fails with LDAP error 50, while HR admin reads, changes, and restores HR-4815. Restrictions persisted after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Anonymous users see no employee records
evidence.summary: Anonymous subtree searches returned zero employee entries before and after both node restarts.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated demonstration credentials are securely provisioned
evidence.summary: Dedicated reader/admin credential files exist in root-only 0700 directories with passwords and DNs mode 0600; no credential values were exposed.

evidence.requirement: Security controls and compatible platform preserved
evidence.summary: RHEL 10 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remain installed; SELinux is Enforcing, firewalld is active, LDAP ingress is limited to node2, and no failed units remain.

Healthy baseline boot ID 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a, safe-reboot acknowledgement and disconnect, changed boot ID 55743d53-bb7c-433b-8617-b70b64b25b0e, then active LDAP listeners, intact data, and remote policy recovery.

Healthy baseline boot ID 2db46909-a020-4fda-b1db-2c3ead04c18a, safe-reboot acknowledgement and disconnect, changed boot ID 584117b1-bbeb-4642-8f95-1d9b731db3f3, then protected credentials, trusted LDAPS access, intact source data, and complete authorization-policy recovery.
